title: Career Paths
paragraphs: “Sakura-chan, now that you don’t have any rivals, this is your chance to get some special attention from Father.”
“Oh, really? Got it!”

After that little exchange, I looked out from the castle terrace toward the town below Siltvelt. I could see the town was quite lively, all things considered. In Melromarc, it’s usually quiet at this time of day.
“Ah, Motoyasu-kun.”
I turned at the sound of his voice, and there stood Father.
“Oh? Father, what brings you out here?”
“Well, nothing in particular—I just couldn’t fall asleep, so I was taking a stroll around the castle.”

Father seems a bit worn out lately. Not only does he spend time with Sakura-chan and Panda, but he’s also been leaning against Zou more often to unwind. It’s important to take it easy every once in a while.
“Are you all right?”
“Yeah, I’m fine.”
Father stood beside me, taking in the panoramic view of the castle town.
“……Gaelion’s return home, huh—”
Father muttered that under his breath.
“Do you want to go home, Father?”

In the first world, Father had categorically stated that he would return home without hesitation once the world was at peace. However, it seems his thoughts gradually changed, and in the end, he stayed. Father from the previous world also saw me off with a similar feeling. Then, Father looks at me with a subtle expression.
“I didn’t mean it that way. I suppose the other ‘me’ that Motoyasu-kun knows probably did want to go back, though.”

Hmm… It seems I was mistaken. Come to think of it, I remembered Father once saying he wanted to explore this world more. I’m not sure exactly which loop that was, but if he doesn’t want to go back, then that must be how he really feels.
“It’s just… I felt a bit nostalgic. It’s only been a few months since I came to this other world, but I realized there are times when I feel that way.”

Hmm… From my perspective, my life back in Japan feels like something from the distant past. But do I feel nostalgic? …Come to think of it, I suppose I do, to some extent. More than that, though, I’m focused on tomorrow. True, from Father’s perspective, my days in this other world haven’t been that long yet.
“It’s been such a continuous string of exciting days that it’s easy to forget, but before I came to this other world, I was a student… Speaking of which, what about you, Motoyasu?”
“Me?”
“Yeah. Ren and Itsuki are high school students, right, given their ages?　Since you’re a college student around the same age as Motoyasu, I was wondering—what was the college you attended like?”
Father seems interested in my student days. Apparently, he says they’re very similar to a galge. But I’m also interested in your student days, Father.
“What was your college life like, Father?”

“Huh? Me? Hmm… Well, I guess I was pretty average in college? I didn’t stand out too much or cause too much of a ruckus—nothing special, nothing terrible. If anything, my social life was mainly online.”
“Oh, come to think of it, Itsuki once called you a ‘net-junkie.’”
“I suppose that’s not wrong… Though I’m a little surprised to hear it from Itsuki’s mouth—but you’re talking about another world, right?”
I nod. Itsuki in this world was a total mess, but there are worlds where he’s actually useful.
“That’s right. So, since Father is such a good cook, did you actually go to a culinary school?”
I’d been wondering about that for a while. Father’s cooking is really delicious, after all. I’m sure he must have attended a famous culinary college.
“Nah? Just a regular third-rate university. Part of the reason was that it was close to home.”
Huh? My guess was off. Just as I was thinking that, Father made a slightly exasperated face.
“Come to think of it, I vaguely remember my family telling me that once I dropped out or graduated from college, I should go to a culinary school…”
“Did you dislike that idea?”
“Not really. I think I just treated it as a safety net, at most.”
“Your restaurant would have been a huge success, I’m sure.”
“I don’t think it would have gone that far, though.”

That said, having tasted Father’s cooking in all sorts of settings, I can say with absolute certainty that it would have been a success. It’s delicious even at low levels and with unrefined skills. In other words, it’s a skill that Father himself possesses.
“According to Itsuki, you said Father comes from the world of cooking manga, didn’t you?”

“I’ve never actually seen any of those mysterious cooking competitions or anything… Oh well. Was there anything particularly noteworthy about my student life? That’s pretty much how I made my choices. With my brain, I just couldn’t study that hard anyway.”
You really underestimate yourself, Father. It’s thanks to you that I learned the Melromarc alphabet. There’s no doubt you’re the kind of person who can achieve anything if you put your mind to it.
“What about you, Motoyasu? It seems like you had quite a romantic college life.”
“That’s true… Come to think of it, I remember there were three major relationships when I decided to go to college.”
“Which university did you attend before coming here?”

“A big university in the city. I was told I had a shot at getting in based on my academic ability, so I applied. It was a prestigious school, the kind people say gives you an edge when looking for a job.”
“Ah… Like the University of Tokyo or something similar?”
“The abbreviation’s different, but I’d say it’s just a notch below that.”
“Motoyasu, you’re pretty smart. And yet… no, intelligence and action are two different things, aren’t they?”
Father just complimented me! That’s right. No matter how smart you are, nothing happens unless you take action. Action is more important than intelligence!
“Wisdom over intelligence, indeed!”
“W-well, something like that…”
“Getting back to the story, well, I ended up moving to Tokyo, got all worked up over a girl, and ended up getting stabbed.”
Since I ended up coming to this other world and discovering true love, I have no regrets. My wish is simply to spend more time with Filo-tan.
“So there was a chance you could’ve gone to the other two places too?”
“That’s right.”
“I wonder what my college life would’ve been like?”

“Hmm… One of them was a large university near my hometown—one of several there. If I’d chosen that one, I’d have ended up going to school with a pig I could call an old friend—who’d come wake me up every morning—and a ridiculously rich pig.”

Since I’d changed schools so often, our connection was a bit tenuous, but when I lived in that town, there was this pig who lived next door—an old acquaintance—who would come by every single morning to wake me up. As for the rich pig… I can’t really remember him. I just vaguely recall meeting him once or twice when I was little.
“It’s kind of… a cliché, isn’t it?”

“There were pigs all over the place claiming to be old friends, weren’t there? Even though they’d only lived in the neighborhood for a few months back when I was in elementary school, they sure did a good job of it.”
“Hmm… I wonder if you were to condense the protagonists of multiple gal games, you’d end up with a background like Motoyasu-kun’s…”
Father is listening with great interest. Well then, let’s talk some more. Father from the first world didn’t seem interested in this sort of thing, so I never had a chance to talk to him about it.

“If I had to say what sets it apart, it’s that the rich jerk I met there was actually incredibly wealthy. He had a lot of connections with business tycoons from various industries, and when I was attending that university, he used to talk about buying up the surrounding land and clearing it so I could go straight from home to school, or even digging a direct underground tunnel.”

“Ah, there used to be characters like that—ridiculously rich—in old manga and gal games, right? Wait, is this actually real…? But if that’s the case, I’m scared to think what’ll happen to the woman who killed Motoyasu.”
It wasn’t a woman who killed me—it was a pig, wasn’t it? Well, the details don’t really matter.
“By the way, back in high school, I got hooked on competitive robot games at that local arcade. That was before I got hooked on Emerald Online.”

I used to practice day and night with a friend. If I’d been attending this university, my passion for those games might have been reignited. Incidentally, this friend—unusually for me—is a guy. Well, he had a slender build and a face as delicate as a woman’s, though.
“Huh—a cyber-mechanical game? Like *Mobile Warrior*?”
I don’t quite understand Father’s explanation, but he’s probably right. It seems every world has games like that.
“Anyway, that’s one of them. The other is… a university my grandfather, who loves history, recommended. He said it was a prestigious, traditional university.”
“So, despite what you say, Motoyasu-kun comes from a pretty good family, huh?”

“It’s not quite that. It’s just that my grandfather recommended it. My grandfather loves the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, the Warring States period, and Chūshingura. Thanks to everything he taught me, history was my strongest subject.”
In that sense, my grandfather really helped me out. I’ve never failed a test on things like historical eras or dates.
“...Hey, Motoyasu, in your version of Japan, are the military commanders actually women?”
“They’re men, aren’t they?”
Why would the military commanders be women? Or rather, historically speaking, I think it’s only in recent years that women’s status and influence have really grown, don’t you think?
“You’re right. It’s not like Japan would go so far as to have female military commanders, is it? I was just wondering—was Motoyasu-kun’s Japan a world where there were fewer men?”

Hmm… It seems that my Japan and Father’s Japan are similar yet different. I know there are differences between Itsuki and Ren’s worlds as well. It’s not that I think I’m strange; those kinds of differences might just exist.

“I did go check out the open houses at every university, just to be sure. As for the one my grandfather recommended… well, for some reason, I was curious about a warehouse, so I peeked inside and saw a large, old mirror—that really stuck with me. I’m sure that must have been the main attraction.”
I suppose my grandfather recommended it to me because it was an item with a certain charm that draws people in.
“Huh… So you went through quite a lot before coming to this world, Motoyasu-kun.”
“That’s all in the past—stories from when I was a foolish man. For me, this world is everything.”
This world, where Filo-tan and Filolial-sama are, is my ultimate joy. I can’t even imagine any other world. I don’t want to go back, either.
“Anyway, I went to a university in the city in search of new horizons. I have no regrets about that decision. After all, it led me to meet Filo-tan and awaken to true love.”
As I say that, my student life so far flashes before my eyes. …Come to think of it, my student days were nothing but romances with pigs—how foolish of me.

Huh? There’s someone in my memory who looks like a woman. That’s strange, isn’t it? Almost everyone I dated back then was supposed to be a pig… As I recalled the person who popped into my mind from head to toe, I mulled over why she wasn’t a pig—and then it hit me.

Come to think of it, this woman… wasn’t a woman at all—she was a man. He was a man with an incredibly slender build who enjoyed cross-dressing, so I mistook him for a woman. He was kind of like Midoriya or Kuro-chan. I’ve had romantic relationships with people like that, too.

Sometimes I knew he was a man from the start, sometimes I found out later, and sometimes I said I still loved him even after realizing it. Thinking about the times I slept with pigs makes me feel nauseous, but as for the times I had relationships with men… I don’t feel particularly bad about them. It’s practically no different from being with a woman.

It’s just like how I cherish Midoriya, Kou, and Kuro-chan, just as I do Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan. With Filo-tan at the top of the pyramid and the great Filolial-sama right below her, I love Filolial-sama just as much. Gender isn’t really a big deal.

With that said, I turn my gaze toward Father. Come to think of it, tFather was the one who stopped me—when I’d gone berserk after remembering Takt—amidst the flames. I can still remember that moment clearly.
“Yeah… I understand how you feel, so—”
After that, I’m pretty sure he said something romantic. That’s right. TFather is that very same father.
“…Motoyasu-kun? What’s wrong?”

Hmm… He isn’t dressed in women’s clothes, but he does look cute. Maybe it’s because he’s a gentle father—unlike the one from the first world—that this aspect stands out more, and I’ve come to recognize it.

Come to think of it, Rival once said he was after Father’s virginity. Since Father already has a panda and an elephant, I assume he’s lost his virginity, but what about his virginity? It wouldn’t be at all surprising if Rival had been aiming for that from the start.
In that case… I, Motoyasu, might be able to lend a hand. I’ll confront Father with the same expression I had when I seduced that man in women’s clothes, and I’ll place my hand on his face.
“Motoyasu-kun? You seem a little off today…”
“You must be exhausted. Let me help you.”
I genuinely want to be there for Father. After all, I’ve helped men in drag before—I know they have all sorts of pent-up desires they want to unleash, and I’ve been there to support them emotionally.
“Huh? Ah… yeah. You’ve helped me out a lot, Motoyasu-kun.”
“That’s not all—I might be able to help you even more.”
I exhale softly into Father’s ear.
“Eek!? It feels just like when Motoyasu-kun licked my neck before!?”
Father seems a little frightened, but momentum is key here. I’ve got to keep pushing.
“Just like you’d lean on a panda or an elephant, it’s okay to lean on me, too, you know?”
“Eh…? Well… um…”

After all, the story is that Father was planning to sleep with Torao. I’m sure Father, feeling hurt, wanted me to do something like this. If I take one more step and push a little harder, I think he’ll sleep with me tonight. Just as I was thinking that—
“Hmm… Naofumi… there you are.”
Sakura-chan came shuffling over, still half-asleep.
“Ah, Sakura-chan! Did I wake you up? Sorry about that. But you saved me.”
Father approached Sakura-chan and spoke to her, as if suddenly snapping back to his senses.
“Well then, let’s go back to your room and get some more sleep. Motoyasu-kun, thanks for talking things over with me.”
“You’re welcome. And Father, I’ll always be here to help you out. Just be careful of that pig and Rival!”
“Um… yeah, thanks.”

Although I had my doubts, I trusted Father to stay on the straight and narrow, so I said goodbye to him that day and went back to my room to sleep. If Sakura-chan had gone to see her Finacée… things might have worked out!
The Ultimate Sakura Block is activated!
